name: AGC 198508 (Hubble)
blurb: AGC 198508, a gas-rich dwarf galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: agc198508-hubble
story: A faint dwarf galaxy rich in hydrogen gas and still forming stars, one of the tiny systems picked out by the ALFALFA survey. Hubble resolved its stars to measure its distance.

claims.text: AGC 198508 is one of the SHIELD II galaxies imaged by Hubble program 13750
SHIELD galaxies are gas-rich, very low-mass galaxies selected from the ALFALFA HI survey, all with recent star formation, probing the faint end of the luminosity function for star-forming galaxies
A tip-of-the-red-giant-branch distance was measured to AGC 198508 from Hubble photometry
